questions.a: Restaurant loyalty software runs a rewards program that encourages guests to come back. Guests earn points, visits or stamps when they order, then redeem rewards in store or online. Most tools also let you send targeted offers by email, SMS or push to bring quiet regulars back.

questions.q: Is a loyalty program worth it for a small restaurant?
questions.a: It often is, because your regulars visit more often, spend more and recommend you to friends. You don't need a big tech budget to start. Small restaurants can use loyalty built into their POS or a simple digital stamp card with no hardware or POS integration.

questions.q: What should I look for in restaurant loyalty software?
questions.a: Check that it integrates with your POS, online ordering and reservation tools, and that guests can earn at one location and redeem at another. Segmentation matters too, so you can spot guests who are about to churn and talk to each group differently. Finally, look for metrics you can act on, like repeat visit rate, days between visits and lifetime value.

questions.q: Should I use my POS's built-in loyalty or a separate platform?
questions.a: Built-in loyalty is simpler, since there's no second tool to log into and no data to sync. The trade-off is that it only works inside that POS ecosystem. Standalone platforms offer deeper segmentation, subscriptions and personalization, which suits multi-location chains with marketing teams.

questions.q: What types of loyalty programs work for restaurants?
questions.a: Common models are spend-based points, visit-based points, tiered memberships and digital stamp cards. Spend-based points suit fine dining, while visit-based points suit a quick-service cafe. Some brands also reward top guests with perks beyond discounts, like reservations or secret menu items, which protects margins.

questions.q: How can loyalty points help recover unhappy guests?
questions.a: Issuing points or a reward when a guest complains about a bad meal or missed points can bring them back. Momos works on top of your existing loyalty software so support agents can issue points, rewards and missed-entry credits from the support thread, within brand-level recovery policies. It then tracks whether those rewards were redeemed and the guest came back.
